method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: The corridor is lettered 'AVE. A OR WATER' inside the roadway I measured on both plates (the G.C.&S.F.R.R. tracks are drawn along it, and '70'' is printed in it on both), and on both it is the 0/100 hundred-block break of the numbered streets: west of it the frontages read 1 3 5 7 9 11 / 2 4 6 8 10 12 and 13 15 ... 23 / 14 16 ... 24 on the Galveston Wharf Co. terminal column, and east of it they read 101 103 ... 111 / 102 104 ... 112 and 113 115 ... 123 / 114 116 ... 124. One block EAST is excluded because that corridor is lettered 'AVE. B OR STRAND' on both plates (sheet 27 roadway 2064.0-2305.2, sheet 33 roadway 2059.1-2301.7, about 1020 px east) and it carries the 100/200 break, with 201 203 205 / 202 204 206 208 printed beyond it. One block WEST is not an avenue at all - it is the wharf front, the Galveston Wharf Co's terminal tracks and yard, with no lettered corridor - so the only candidate confusion is with the Strand, which the lettering and the hundred-block runs exclude. The block column between the wharf front and Water St is continuous across the shared 15TH ST seam with consecutive block numbers: sheet 27 has blocks 733 (13th-14th) and 734 (14th-15th), sheet 33 continues with 735 (15th-16th) and 736 (16th-17th); the Water-to-Strand column likewise runs 673, 674 on sheet 27 and 675, 676 on sheet 33, with avenue-face addresses 1301-1327 / 1401-1427 on sheet 27 and 1501-1528 / 1601-1622 on sheet 33. Sheet 27's south margin prints '33' and sheet 33's north margin prints '27', confirming the two are stacked on 15TH ST. Corroboration: drafted roadway width 213.2 native px on sheet 27 and 211.7 on sheet 33, matching the printed 70'. MEASUREMENT: midpoint of the two facing block lines, read off the green native ruler in the band immediately adjacent to the shared 15TH ST seam and averaged over the two crops that show the corridor - sheet 27 faces 1060.5/1273.7 (cand1) and 1057.9/1271.1 (cand2), sheet 33 faces 1053.4/1265.1 (cand3) and 1050.0/1261.7 (cand2). Implied cross-plate shift 8.2 px. PLATE DISAGREEMENT, recorded not reconciled: the same reads taken on the Strand give a shift of only 3.9 px (sheet 27 centers 2186.6/2184.6, sheet 33 2183.1/2180.4), i.e. sheet 33 draws the Water-to-Strand span about 4-5 px (0.45 percent) wider than sheet 27, so this control carries roughly +/-2 px of corridor-choice sensitivity. Ave A is reported rather than the Strand because its drafted width agrees more closely between the plates (1.5 px vs about 2 px) and its identity is pinned by the sharpest evidence, the wharf front on one side and the 0/100 break on the other. NOTE: no reported coordinate is a detection candidate - the candidates on both sheets (27: 748/1763/2778, 33: 546/1561/2576) are mid-block lines, not avenues.
